To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the three damage modes for all-ceramic crowns are cone cracking, flexural fracture, and plastic deformation.

the three damage modes of ceramics are: 1) Hertzian cracking for the thinnest layers (less than 0.5 mm) 2) Yielding for the intermediate thickness (0.5-1 mm) 3) Flexure for the thickest layers (greater than 1 mm)

the damage modes for ceramic restorations are: Hertzian cone fracture for thin layers and for thicker layers with flaws in the outer aspect, pseudo-plastic flow for intermediate thickness layers and for thicker ceramic layers with flaws in both the inner and outer aspect and flexural fracture for thick layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fundamental understanding of damage mechanisms in ceramics and their application to clinical practice.
developing the understanding of ceramic fracture modes in the molar crown.
the development of an understanding of the damage modes of dental ceramics in order to predict clinical performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical performance of all-ceramic crowns is excellent.
ceramic crowns of 2 mm thickness are not recommended.
ceramic crowns are a viable and esthetic alternative to metal ceramic crowns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ceramic crown failure is a function of material properties, microstructure, and the clinical situation.
the clinical performance of ceramic crowns can be predicted by the above relationships and that the clinical performance is not a function of the luting agent or the cement thickness.
ceramic layer crowns can be made to be very reliable if the above factors are considered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ceramic crown failure is related to the damage modes of the material and the geometry of the crown.
the clinical success of a given dental restoration depends not only on its design but on the materials used and how they are used in the design.
the molar crown is an ideal testing ground for dental ceramics.
